Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 18)
Topic: Brahmacharya, Part 2 — Character (Charitra), Not Conduct (Aacharan): How God's Tattva Actually Awakens

Sour ce: A short Ashaeiynn Foundation training video (video transcript, ~1 1 min) — a dir ect instructional monologue rather than a live satsang Q&A. Explicitly framed as the second video in a short sub-series on brahmacharya (the first being Session 17's teaching on sex, nightfall, and sadhna); this session r edefines brahmacharya itself, corr ecting the common assumption that it means following a strict set of conduct rules. Purpose: Chatbot knowledge — English version. Note on conversational content: this is a short, dir ect training monologue with no sangat back-and-forth — ther e is no separate curated conversational supplement for this session (see closing note).
1. THE QUESTION THIS SESSION ANSWERS

Does brahmacharya r eally mean following the exact conduct described in the Vedas and Puranas — and if a practitioner can't follow all of it, does that mean siddhis, shakti, and darshan of devtas ar e simply out of r each? This session sets out to correct that assumption directly .
2. THE COMMON (INCOMPLETE) UNDERSTANDING OF BRAHMACHARYA

The familiar definition: brahmacharya = "Brahm ka aacharan" — the conduct/behavior of Brahm (God). Under this view , a practitioner must follow a specific set of principles (for example: of fering yachaman/prayer before eating, giving thanks after eating, acting only with viniyoga and sankalp) in order to be considered an "achaarya" of that practice. In practice, almost no one can consistently follow every rule in this set — which raises the question of whether falling short of full conduct means falling short of spiritual attainment.
3. THE CORRECTION — BRAHMACHARYA MEANS "BRAHM KA CHARITRA," NOT "BRAHM KA AACHARAN"

Bhaiya states this corr ection was taught to him dir ectly by his own Guru: brahmacharya does not mean the conduct of Brahm — it means the CHARACTER (charitra) of Brahm. Your character should be God-like. What you do or don't do in terms of outward conduct does NOT define you. What matters is that your character (charitra) should not be "malin" (impure/tainted). If your character is clean, nothing can stop you fr om attaining shakti — full stop.
4. WHY THE "PERFECT ROUTINE" ASSUMPTION DOESN'T HOLD UP

A common assumption: if I wake at 5am, meditate, do all my duties, r emain fully in brahmacharya, and avoid looking at women, God will meet me. Bhaiya directly challenges this: if this were actually how it worked, everyone who followed
such a routine would already have attained it. This is not how it actually works.
5. WHERE CHARACTER (CHARITRA) ACTUALLY COMES FROM

Brahm ka charitra is born specifically when God's tattva (divine element) awakens within a practitioner's body . Shakti is received only once this brahm charitra has formed in the body — and charitra, in turn, forms only once God's tattva has been born within the body . This is presented as a precise, mechanical sequence: tattva → charitra → shakti — not a matter of outward discipline alone.
6. HOW GOD'S TATTVA IS ACTUALLY BORN — THE FULL MECHANISM

When a practitioner begins mantra jaap, the body's 12 "goles" (cir cles) and 7 chakras begin to fill first. The mantra then cir culates continuously ar ound the practitioner's aura mandal. Over a certain period, the mantra's protective "layers" (also described as shields) increase. Once roughly 10-12 such shields have formed, the devta governing that specific mantra's particular lok (r ealm) comes to personally assess the practitioner — taking stock of them and qualifying them for the next stage. Once the devta appr oves the practitioner , they deposit their own tarang (wave/vibration) into the practitioner's body . This tarang circulates fully throughout the practitioner's body — a phenomenon directly observed through drishti, both by Bhaiya and by others who have had their own drishti opened. This circulating tarang eventually settles at a specific chakra, and a tattva begins forming ther e — taking on a cir cular shape. This is what is called "God's tattva," and it is this tattva that automatically , spontaneously produces brahm charitra — with no rules or conduct-following required for this specific step.
7. WHAT HAPPENS ONCE GOD'S TATTVA IS AWAKENED

Once this tattva is awakened in a practitioner's body , that bhaav (devotional essence) and tattva never leave them again — regardless of outward cir cumstance. The session states plainly that such a person could eat meat, live anywhere, or live in any manner , and the tattva would still remain intact within them, ready to be reawakened with a single call. This is explicitly contrasted with a person who spends years following brahm ka aacharan (conduct rules) alone — such conduct-based effort, on its own, cannot r eliably achieve what tattva-awakening achieves. Understanding this distinction — character versus conduct — is described as critically important, and the session repeatedly warns against mixing the two up, noting that "much of the world" conflates them.
8. WHY GOD'S TATTVA IS THE FOUNDATION OF FURTHER SPIRITUAL GROWTH

This same tattva is what actually connects a person to the devtas — and it is fr om this connection that a practitioner's gr owth in gyaan (spiritual knowledge) genuinely begins. Again, this is explicitly not the "Brahm ka aacharan" (conduct) framework — it is the tattva-driven charitra framework.
9. SUPPOR TING EVIDENCE — TATTVA COMES BEFORE DRISHTI, NOT AFTER

Bhaiya cites a dir ect, checkable pattern fr om the past year of practitioners whose drishti has opened: appr oximately 99% of these practitioners r eceived God's tattva FIRST , with drishti opening only afterward — not the reverse. This pattern is described as verifiable and has been documented and shared (e.g., on YouT ube). The implication for a practitioner who feels discouraged that they "can't follow" a strict conduct r egimen: this concern is based on mixing up conduct and character , and should not be a sour ce of worry — the tattva-first pathway does not depend on perfect conduct.
10. GAINING A SPECIFIC DEVTA'S CHARACTER REQUIRES THAT DEVTA'S OWN PERMISSION FIRST

To develop the charitra of any specific devta, a practitioner must first receive that devta's own permission/order (aagya). Without it, a practitioner cannot receive that devta's tattva into their body — this is described as one of the genuine rules governing the process. Befor e this permission can be granted, the practitioner must first please/win over that same divine figur e ("rijhana"). As the teaching puts it: "Prabhu kripa karenge, binu Hari kripa mile hi nahin; santan bina kripa ke sant nahi milte" (grace from the Lord is what makes this possible in the first place; without a saint's grace, God's tattva cannot be attained). This is of fered as the actual gateway condition behind tattva reception — not a matter of independently "manufacturing" one's own character through willpower alone.
1 1. HOW ASHAEIYNN ACTUALLY DEVELOPS THIS IN PRACTITIONERS

Ashaeiynn Foundation's appr oach (formerly deliver ed through what was called the "Foundation Course," now updated) does NOT put members into strict brahmacharya, an especially strict diet, or ask them to give up ordinary aspects of life. Instead, the pr ocess runs entir ely thr ough mantra shakti , working through this sequence: filling the body's first 12 goles, establishing bodily raksha-suraksha (protection), triggering astral activation in the body , aura shielding, chakra jagriti (awakening), and finally tattva prapti (attainment of the tattva). It is through this sequence — not thr ough externally imposed conduct rules — that brahm ka charitra is actually cultivated in a practitioner .
12. WHAT BECOMES POSSIBLE ONCE BRAHM KA CHARITRA IS PRESENT

Once this charitra is pr esent, a practitioner can sit anywher e and see or understand whatever they choose to focus on. The teaching states plainly: there is no vidya beyond such a person's r each, and no shakti beyond their reach — a practitioner can attain any vidya, by building both the grahan shakti (capacity to receive it) and the prayog shakti (capacity to actually use it).
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

1. Brahmacharya is commonly misunderstood as "Brahm ka aacharan" (following God-like conduct/rules) — this session corrects that to "Brahm ka charitra" (having a God-like character), as taught directly by Bhaiya's own Guru. 2. What a practitioner does or doesn't do outwardly (conduct) does not define them — what matters is that their character (charitra) remains unclouded ("not malin"). 3. The assumption that a perfect external routine (early rising, meditation, strict continence) guarantees meeting God doesn't hold up — if it did, everyone who followed such a routine would already have attained it. 4. Shakti is received only once brahm ka charitra has formed in the body , and charitra forms only once God's tattva has been born in the body — this is a precise sequence: tattva → charitra → shakti. 5. God's tattva is born through a specific mechanism: mantra jaap fills the body's 12 goles and 7 chakras; the mantra circulates in the aura mandal, building up 10-12 protective "shields" over time; the mantra's governing devta then personally assesses and approves the practitioner; upon approval, the devta deposits their own tarang (wave) into the practitioner's body , which circulates and settles at a chakra, forming God's tattva there. 6. Once God's tattva is awakened, it never leaves the practitioner regardless of outward lifestyle circumstances, and can be reawakened with a single call — something years of conduct-following alone cannot reliably achieve. 7. This same tattva is what connects a practitioner to the devtas, and is the actual starting point for growth in spiritual knowledge (gyaan) — not conduct-following on its own.

8. A verifiable pattern from the past year: roughly 99% of practitioners whose drishti opened received God's tattva FIRST , with drishti opening only afterward — not the reverse. 9. Developing a specific devta's charitra requires first receiving that devta's own permission — which itself depends on that devta's grace (kripa); tattva reception is a matter of grace, not independent willpower alone. 10. Ashaeiynn's own method does not impose strict brahmacharya, restrictive diets, or lifestyle renunciation — it works entirely through mantra shakti (goles, raksha-suraksha, astral activation, aura shielding, chakra jagriti, tattva prapti) to cultivate brahm ka charitra directly . 1 1. Once brahm ka charitra is present, no vidya or shakti is beyond a practitioner's reach — they can attain any vidya by building both the capacity to receive it (grahan shakti) and the capacity to use it (prayog shakti).

Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 18, English)
Brahmacharya, Part 2 — Character (Charitra), Not Conduct (Aacharan)
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn Foundation training module. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. Does brahmacharya mean I have to follow all the conduct rules described in the Vedas and Puranas — and if I can't, am I missing out on shakti and darshan? A: Jai Siya Ram! No — this is exactly the misunderstanding this session corrects. The common definition treats brahmacharya as "Brahm ka aacharan," a strict set of conduct rules to follow . But Bhaiya was taught directly by his own Guru that brahmacharya actually means "Brahm ka charitra" — character that is God-like, not a checklist of conduct. What you do or don't do outwardly doesn't define you; what matters is that your character stays unclouded.

Q2. If I wake up early , meditate, do all my duties, and stay strictly celibate, will that guarantee I meet God? A: Not necessarily — and this exact assumption is directly challenged in this teaching. If following a perfect external routine like this guaranteed divine attainment, everyone who followed it would already have attained it. That's simply not how it works in practice.

Q3. So wher e does r eal spiritual character (charitra) actually come fr om? A: It comes from a specific, precise sequence: God's tattva (divine element) must first awaken within your body; only once that tattva is present does brahm ka charitra form; and only once that charitra is present do you actually receive shakti. It's tattva → charitra → shakti — not outward discipline alone.

Q4. How does God's tattva actually get "born" in a practitioner's body? A: It happens through a specific mechanism. When you begin mantra jaap, your body's 12 goles and 7 chakras start to fill first. The mantra then circulates continuously through your aura mandal, and over time its protective "layers" or shields increase. Once roughly 10-12 shields have formed, the devta governing that specific mantra's realm personally comes to assess and approve the practitioner . Once approved, that devta deposits their own tarang (wave) into the practitioner's body — this tarang circulates fully through the body and eventually settles at a chakra, forming a circular tattva there. This is what's called "God's tattva."

Q5. Once this tattva is awakened in me, is it fragile — could I lose it by living an "imperfect" life? A: No — once this tattva is awakened, it never leaves, regardless of outward lifestyle. The teaching states plainly that such a person could eat meat, live anywhere, or live in any manner , and the tattva and its bhaav (devotional essence) would remain fully intact, ready to reawaken with a single call. This is explicitly contrasted with years of conduct-following alone, which cannot reliably achieve the same result.

Q6. Why is it so important not to mix up "conduct" and "character" her e? A: Because much of the world conflates the two — assuming that following conduct rules IS what builds brahmacharya. In reality , character (charitra) comes from tattva awakening, which happens through a specific mantra-based mechanism, not primarily through outward behavioral discipline. Confusing the two can lead a sincere practitioner to feel discouraged that they "aren't doing enough," when in fact conduct was never the actual determining factor .

Q7. What does this tattva actually do for a practitioner beyond just "existing" in them? A: This same tattva is what genuinely connects a person to the devtas — and it's from this connection that real growth in spiritual knowledge (gyaan) begins. It's the actual functional bridge to deeper learning, not conduct-following on its own.

Q8. Is ther e any r eal evidence that tattva comes befor e drishti, rather than the other way ar ound? A: Yes — Bhaiya cites a directly checkable pattern from the past year of practitioners whose drishti has opened: roughly 99% of them received God's tattva FIRST, with drishti opening only afterward. This pattern has been documented and shared publicly (e.g., on YouT ube), and it directly supports the tattva-before-drishti sequence taught in this session.

Q9. Can I just decide on my own to build a specific devta's character in myself? A: Not entirely on your own — to develop any specific devta's charitra, you must first receive that devta's own permission (aagya); without it, you cannot receive their tattva into your body . And that permission itself depends on first pleasing/winning over that divine figure through devotion — as the teaching puts it, grace from the Lord is what makes this possible in the first place, and without a saint's grace, God's tattva cannot be attained. This is a matter of grace, not willpower alone.

Q10. Does Ashaeiynn r equire its members to follow strict brahmacharya, a special diet, or give up parts of their ordinary life? A: No — Ashaeiynn's approach doesn't put members into strict brahmacharya, an unusually strict diet, or ask them to renounce ordinary life. The entire process runs through mantra shakti: filling the body's first 12 goles, establishing bodily raksha-suraksha (protection), triggering astral activation, aura shielding, chakra jagriti (awakening), and finally tattva prapti (attainment). It's this sequence — not imposed conduct rules — that actually cultivates brahm ka charitra.

Q1 1. What becomes possible once a practitioner genuinely has brahm ka charitra? A: At that point, a practitioner can sit anywhere and see or understand whatever they choose to focus on. The teaching states there is no vidya and no shakti beyond such a person's reach — they can attain any vidya by building both the capacity to receive it (grahan shakti) and the capacity to actually use it (prayog shakti).

Q12. I feel discouraged because I can't follow every conduct rule I've r ead about — should I be worried this is holding me back? A: No — this concern is based on exactly the conduct-versus-character confusion this session addresses directly . The tattva-first pathway toward brahm ka charitra does not depend on perfect outward conduct; it depends on the mantra-shakti-driven process of tattva awakening. Worrying about imperfect conduct in this context is misplaced.
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 18 additions)

When a user expresses guilt or discouragement about failing to follow strict conduct rules (diet, routine, celibacy), immediately introduce the charitra-vs-aacharan distinction from this session — reassure them that character (via tattva awakening), not conduct, is what actually matters here. Never present Ashaeiynn's path as requiring strict brahmacharya, special diet, or lifestyle renunciation — this session explicitly states the opposite; the mechanism is mantra shakti (goles, raksha-suraksha, astral activation, aura shielding, chakra jagriti, tattva prapti), not imposed conduct. When explaining how shakti or drishti is attained, use the precise tattva → charitra → shakti sequence from this session rather than implying it comes from conduct/discipline alone. If a user asks about attaining a specific devta's blessing or character , clarify that this requires that devta's own permission/grace first — frame this as a matter of devotion and grace, not self-willed achievement. Keep this session's teaching distinct from Session 17's veerya/nightfall mechanics — Session 17 addresses whether sex/nightfall disrupts sadhna; this session redefines brahmacharya itself as character rather than conduct. Use whichever is relevant to the user's specific question, and note the two are companion teachings when both are relevant. Cite the "~99% tattva-before-drishti" pattern only as a documented observation from this teaching, not as an absolute universal law. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
